correctness.rationale: For each ordered dimension profile the stabilizer is the product of the block general linear groups (including the trivial size-zero factors). Multiplying the orbit size by the number of blockwise nilpotents cancels all q-powers on division by the total nilpotent count, giving (1). The latter count can also be derived directly: partition all endomorphisms by the canonical nilpotent/invertible Fitting splitting and divide by |GL_n| to get 1/Q_n = sum_{d=0}^n (#nilpotents in dimension d)/|GL_d|; first differences give the required q^(n²−n). The error per profile in replacing the ratio by Q_infty^(1−k) is O(q^(−n)+sum_i q^(−r_i)), summing to O(n^(k−2)) at fixed q,k. This proves the mean and gives O(1/n) total variation on the discrete profile space after normalizing pair weights; the uniform lattice simplex converges weakly to Dirichlet(1,…,1). This is not a conditional-uniform splitting law under a uniform matrix. Indecomposability is exactly one Jordan block, so exactly those matrices attain the minimum k. Their orbit gives (3); strict majority follows for q≥2 and n≥3 by bounding the product below by (3/4)(7/8)(1−sum_{i≥4}2^(−i))=147/256; n=1,2 are immediate. In k=2 the invariant complementary spaces and commuting projections are bijective. Independent finite reproduction: python3 /workspace/branches/125cefa1-8276-4ce4-8c93-941c6f042ab1/independent_counts.py (output independent_counts.out in the same directory). Direct matrix/idempotent enumeration matched all k=2 ranks and k=3 profiles at (n,q)=(2,2),(3,2),(2,3), including 64 nilpotents, rank totals 64,112,112,64 and 42 regular nilpotents at (3,2). Those checks do not certify the limits or constitute formal verification.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The total nilpotent count is an input, not a theorem on splitting distributions. Nilpotent partners are different counting objects from commuting idempotents (the zero map is the only nilpotent idempotent); the inspected pair census does not give a dominating census for compatible splittings.

evidence: The known regular probability immediately gives (3) and its median interpretation once indecomposability is identified with minimum splitting count. The known total count plus orbit–stabilizer gives the exact weight; the summable boundary error, normalization under pair sampling and simplex limit are the additional calculation.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Credit all direct prior consequences, including the regular probability specialized at A=0. The known inputs do not themselves describe the two-measure comparison or give a uniform-composition approximation for compatible pairs; those require identifying and analyzing the actual profile weights.

evidence: The exact profile weight equals the Gaussian multinomial at q^(-1); k=2 sums to the Rogers–Szegő evaluation H_n(1;q^(-1)).

Aggarwal–Ram p. 1 and Prasad–Ram p. 2 treat splitting subspaces defined using iterates, not individually invariant summands. The fixed-two-block Resultary finding counts image Jordan profiles of commuting idempotents and has parity-dependent theta limits.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Projection and ordered invariant complement are exact equivalents, so records counting such idempotents were compared; fixed Jordan type and image Jordan profile do not give the full annealed dimension law. A direct sum of iterates of one space is not a change of notation for this problem.

value.rationale: A natural statistic of nilpotent centralizers (idempotent ranks or several invariant direct summands) has sharply different behavior under two canonical measures. The exact jointly indexed mean explains the difference and supplies the lattice rate and the continuum profile law even when a strict majority of uniform matrices has no nontrivial split. The increment is this quantitative comparison, not the known regular probability or a renamed Gaussian coefficient alone.
